title: You brought something to God…
paragraphs:
You brought something to God…
—but deep down, you knew it cost you nothing.
And somehow, you still expected Him to bless it.
That’s where Malachi 1 hits like a hammer.

Because this isn’t about atheists.
This is about people who still show up…
but stopped honoring God in secret.

Because what looked holy in public…
was hollow in private.
Here’s the tension you can’t ignore:

What if you’ve been doing all the right things…
with the wrong heart?

What if your prayers sound right…
but your devotion is divided?

What if your worship is loud…
but your surrender is silent?
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable.
They were just giving Him what was left.

Blind animals.
Lame sacrifices.
Polluted offerings.
And God calls it out—no filter, no softness:

“A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is my honor?”
— Malachi 1:6
Where is His honor… in your life?
This is the part we don’t like to admit.

We say God is first…
but check Him last.

We sing “You are worthy”…
but give Him distracted attention.

We lift our hands in church…
but hold back our obedience in private.

We give God time…
but never our priorities.

We offer Him presence…
without surrender.

Not just what you bring—
but what it costs you.
Because real worship always costs something.

Your pride.
Your comfort.
Your control.
Your hidden sin.
And here’s the truth that stings:

Empty worship is not neutral.
It is dishonor.

It tells God,
“You are not worth my best.”
This is where shame creeps in.

Moments where God got the leftovers.
Where convenience replaced reverence.
Where routine replaced relationship.
Because Malachi is not just a confrontation.

The Gospel doesn’t say:
“Try harder. Bring a better offering.”

You could never bring a perfect offering…
so God brought one for you.

The sacrifice Israel failed to give…
and we still fail to give.

“He committed no sin, neither was deceit found in his mouth.”
— 1 Peter 2:22

Where your worship is inconsistent—
He was faithful.

Where your heart wanders—
He remained obedient.

Where your offering is stained—
His is spotless.
And here’s the scandal of grace:

God accepted Jesus…
so He could accept you.

Not because your worship is perfect—
but because Christ is.
Grace is not permission to stay empty.
Grace is power to become real.

Because when you truly see Jesus—
you don’t want to give leftovers anymore.

“Present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship.”
— Romans 12:1

From performance… to presence.
From routine… to relationship.
From leftovers… to lordship.
What have you been giving God lately?
Because God is not after your perfection.
And the invitation is still open.

Not when you “fix yourself.”
Not when you “feel ready.”

“Lord… I’ve given You what was easy.
I’ve held back what costs me.
I’ve honored You with words…
but not always with my life.”

“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
— 1 John 1:9
This is the beauty of the Gospel:

Even your empty worship…
can become a new beginning.
If this stirred something in you…
